picks.note: Answered: 1316 and the patrician couple in two sources, the founders described, not named, their dates in one source alone; the Stein-Harfe in sole ownership on the house's pages and the VDP's; the sweet Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese is in others. The harp etymology and the name Harpfe were not found and are not told. The making follows the house's sheet of 2024, a sheet of 2016 giving steel, so the method is not timeless.

picks.why: Bürgstadt family estate of the Mainviereck on iron rich red sandstone, the red side of Franken, winegrowers there since 1638 by its own history; the Hundsrück, entered again in Franken's official register of vineyards in 2010 after the law of 1971 had folded it into the Centgrafenberg, is the Grosse Lage the house calls its flagship site.
picks.note: Answered: the house's own pages call the Hundsrück its flagship site, so it leads over the Centgrafenberg, which is in others with the Frühburgunder; the return of 2010 was the official register's, not the VDP's. The house's namesake is not dated. Open: when the Hundsrück was first bottled alone, not found; the house cites a document of 1525, the record keeping the VDP's tax record of 1564. The family's living members are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: The princely Castell estate on the western edge of the Steigerwald, on gypsum Keuper; the Schlossberg below the castle, held by the estate alone, gives its Silvaner Grosses Gewächs, and the house tells of the first Silvaner recorded in Germany, set at the foot of that hill on 6 April 1659.
picks.note: Answered: the planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's archive, borne out by Wines of Germany and told as the house's account (Wikipedia gives 5 April); the Schlossberg is held alone; the house writes its name Fürstlich Castell'sches Domänenamt. The family's history runs from a presumed ancestor of 1057, with no living name. Open: the house's five years in the castle cellar before release, one sheet only and not told.

picks.why: Schwaigern estate of the counts of Neipperg, whose own tradition holds that the family brought Lemberger to Württemberg in the eighteenth century; the Ruthe, held by the house whole on Gipskeuper of the Heuchelberg, is the Grosse Lage of its Lemberger Grosses Gewächs, with the Schlossberg beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the family's counts are dated (1726, 1821) in two sources; the tie to Saint-Émilion is told as the purchase of 1971 by a branch of the family, with no living name; the Lemberger tradition is told as the house's, not a record; the Ruthe Riesling is in others below Grosses Gewächs, not as a GG. The heads of the family are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Fellbach family estate on the edge of Stuttgart that dates its vines to an ancestor of 1492; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs from Gips Marienglas, the site at Untertürkheim on gypsum Keuper that the family bought in 1973 and calls its flagship site, shows the white side of a red region.
picks.note: Answered: Marienglas names the clear crystal of gypsum; the label reads Untertürkheimer Gips Marienglas. The swap to the Fellbacher Lämmler Lemberger GG was proposed by the author and refused by the refuter: the house's own page calls the Gips its flagship site and no two sources lead with the Lämmler Lemberger, which stays in others; the plan stands. The VDP's figures for its separate Gips page are not this site's and are not given. The family's living members, and the head of 1955 whose status is unknown, are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Fellbach grower's estate of 1997, its own bottles out from 1998, built on Spätburgunder and Lemberger from the Keuper of the Kappelberg; its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs comes from old vines in the Brenner, a parcel within the Lämmler, Fellbach's Grosse Lage.
picks.note: Answered: the Lämmler Spätburgunder GG is in the VDP's and Decanter's listings; 1997 is the house's, the VDP's and two others' (one directory 1996); the founder is said, never named, and is listed in people.json. The teacher of 1858 is cut, the year kept as the founding of the Fellbach co-operative. Open: Hans Schnaitmann of 1550 rests on the house's page alone, told as its account.

picks.why: Bönnigheim family estate that dates its vines there to 1510, its leading reds raised in small oak since 1985 by its own account; its Lemberger Grosses Gewächs comes from the Michaelsberg at Cleebronn, the lone hill of the Zabergäu crowned by a Romanesque church, the label printing Cleebronner Michaelsberg.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP's Michaelsberg page and the listings bear out the Lemberger GG, first with the 2010 vintage, the label printing Cleebronner Michaelsberg and earlier bottlings St. Michaelsfeder; no swap was needed. The son's takeover of 2013 and Kreation of 1990 are cut, unsourced. Open: 1985 for the barriques is the house's account. The father and son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Remstal estate at Stetten east of Stuttgart, begun by its namesake in 1949 and carried on by his son from 1968 and his grandson from 2014; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs from the Pulvermächer, an old terraced slope of Keuper sandstone below the Yburg ruin, shows the Rems valley's white side.
picks.note: Answered: Falstaff and the house's sheets list the Stettener Pulvermächer Riesling GG; the soil is the VDP's, lean sandstone and coloured marl of the Keuper; the name is the VDP's reading, an old word for a blaster of the neighbouring quarry. The founder's dates were not found in two sources, so none is given. Open: the VDP gives two height ranges, the record saying about 330 to 370 metres. The family's living members are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Malterdingen family estate of the Breisgau, of 1987 when the founder left the cooperative to bottle the family's wine, his Spätburgunder made in the manner of Burgundy on limestone; the Bienenberg, where by the VDP's account Cistercian monks grew Spätburgunder in the fourteenth century, is the Grosse Lage of its Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: 1987 in the library, Decanter and wein.plus; the founder's death in June 2014 at fifty five with Decanter, his birth year not found in two sources, so he stays undated; his heirs are listed in people.json and never named. Wildenstein is a Grosse Lage of its own in the VDP's list, its GG in others. Malterdinger as an old local name for Pinot Noir is not told. Open: the barrel time rests on importers' sheets.

picks.why: Ihringen family estate of the Kaiserstuhl, begun in 1935 by a country doctor and built up by his son; the Häusleboden, a parcel in the Wanne of the Winklerberg named for the family's vineyard hut, on volcanic rock, gives its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: 1935 and the doctor are the house's and the VDP's; the label prints Winklerberg Häusleboden and Winklerberg Wanne Häusleboden by year; the Grauburgunder of the hill is no longer claimed in the why, unsourced in the record. The walled terraces and the doctor's wartime recall were not found and are cut. Open: the élevage is Falstaff's for 2020 alone. The family's living members, and the doctor's son whose status is unsettled, are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Oberbergen family estate of the Kaiserstuhl, tied to the Schwarzer Adler, whose kitchen won its first Michelin star in 1969, and by its own account taking its lead from the dry wines of France across the Rhine; its Grauburgunder Grosses Gewächs from the Schlossberg at Achkarren shows the region's white Pinot.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP's Schlossberg page lists the Achkarrer Schlossberg as a Grosse Lage for the house and Falstaff lists the GG over many vintages, so the merge read's condition holds and the pick stands. Franz Keller the elder is named with his dates (1927 to 2007); the estate joined the VDP in 2014. Founded stays empty: the house gives 1892 and the turn of the century. The present head and his son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Neuweier estate by Baden-Baden in the Ortenau, Riesling planted in 1785 by the castle's lord by local accounts; its Mauerberg Riesling goes into the Bocksbeutel, the flask otherwise kept for Franken, by an old right whose origin the accounts tell two ways.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP names the Grosse Lage Mauerberg Mauerwein; the lord of 1785 stays undescribed by name, his dates resting on wein.plus alone; the sale of 2012 is told with no living name. Neuweier and a few neighbouring villages of the Rebland are among the few places outside Franken that may use the Bocksbeutel; no closed list is given, the Weinverordnung itself not read. Open: the cellar's vessels, accounts differing. The owner and an earlier figure of the estate are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Efringen-Kirchen family estate of the Markgräflerland near Basel, founded by a couple of the village in 1991 or 1992, outside the VDP and bottling much of its range as Landwein; Jaspis 10hoch4 is its Gutedel, the Markgräflerland's own grape, from old vines on limestone and long on its lees in wood.
picks.note: Answered: Falstaff lists Jaspis 10hoch4 Gutedel and later 10hoch4 Gutedel, one wine under two labels, told in a trap; the founder is said, never named, and listed in people.json. Open: what 10hoch4 means, unsettled, so not told; why the house bottles as Landwein, not told; no primary source was reached, every fact resting on two secondary ones; the cask size is not claimed.

picks.why: Bacharach family estate at the Hahnenhof; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from the Hahn, a steep slate slope by the Rhine at Bacharach.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The VDP lists the Hahn as an Erste Lage while Falstaff prints the GG as Bacharach Im Hahn: confirm the classification and the label's form for the years taught. The house's namesake only with dates from two sources; the family with no names.

picks.why: Steeg family estate in a side valley above Bacharach, known also for traditional method Riesling Sekt; the St. Jost, a VDP Grosse Lage of slate, gives its Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The VDP's page is the primary for the site and Falstaff lists the GG: confirm the label's form and the Sekt in two sources; the Wolfshöhle goes in others.

picks.why: Spay family estate on the Bopparder Hamm, the long loop of the Rhine at Boppard; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from the Mandelstein, with the Feuerlay beside it.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Falstaff lists both the Mandelstein and the Feuerlay GG: confirm in two sources which leads and the label's form. The estate carries a living grower's name: say the family.

picks.why: Spay family estate making mostly dry and off dry Riesling from the Bopparder Hamm; the Feuerlay, a slate slope of the Hamm, is the site it is known by, in dry and sweet Prädikat styles.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Falstaff lists Bopparder Hamm Feuerlay Riesling Auslese: name the Prädikat the record teaches after the plan's words, from two sources, and say the family with no names.

picks.why: Oberwesel family estate of the slate gorge whose dry and off dry Rieslings come from the Engehöll and the Oelsberg; the Engehöll is the site it is known by.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not searched in this run: the region record names the Engehöll and the Oelsberg; confirm in two sources that the house still makes the Engehöll Riesling, whether as a Grosses Gewächs, and the label's form, else propose a swap with the checker.

picks.why: Stammersdorf estate with vines on the Bisamberg and the Nussberg, farmed biodynamically, that argued for the city's field blend as a fine wine; its Gemischter Satz from the Nussberg is that blend from one Ried.
picks.note: Confirm in two sources the house's part in the DAC of the 2013 vintage and the label's form for the years taught. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Heiligenstadt Heuriger house, recorded as a farm in 1683 by its own account, where Ludwig van Beethoven (1770 to 1827) lodged in 1817; Weisser Marmor is its Riesling from the Nussberg, the city's Riesling bottled alone.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house's own page gives 1683: confirm the Beethoven stay of 1817 in two sources and the label's form (Weisser or Weißer Marmor); its Gemischter Satz from Ried Langteufel and Ried Preussen on the Nussberg goes in others. Tell the sale of 2006 as history with no living name.

picks.why: Grinzing estate on the slopes below the Cobenzl, tied to the City of Vienna; its Gemischter Satz from the Ried Reisenberg is the city's field blend from one of its named sites.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Falstaff lists the wine under Weingut Wien Cobenzl: confirm how the house writes its name, and tell the city's tie to the estate as history with its year from two sources, never as a present owner.

picks.why: Jedlersdorf family estate on the Bisamberg, on the Danube's left bank, with a large Heuriger; its Gemischter Satz from the Wiesthalen, an Erste Lage of the Österreichische Traditionsweingüter, is the left bank's field blend from one site.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Falstaff lists the Ried Wiesthalen year after year with the ÖTW's Erste Lage mark: write the level by its name only. Confirm the house's age and its Heuriger in two sources, and say the family with no names.

picks.why: Mauer family estate of the city's southern vineyards, farmed organically; its Gemischter Satz from the Kaasgraben is one of the field blends the city names by its site.

picks.why: Estate founded in 1997 at Agios Panteleimon on the Amyndeon plateau; its Reserve Vieilles Vignes comes from the Barba Yannis block, ungrafted bush vines of Xinomavro planted in 1919 that phylloxera never reached.

Confirmed in the thin run: the wine is PDO Amyndeon, from one block of ungrafted bush vines planted in 1919 (an American drinks site's account of the estate and a merchant), with two years in French oak and a year in bottle for one vintage by its American importer. The label's words vary by source and by year (Xinomavro Reserve Vieilles Vignes Single Block Barba Yannis by two merchants, Barba Yannis Reserve Vieilles Vignes Xinomavro by a British critic's site, Ecosystem in earlier years), so the pick holds the block's name alone: give the label in full for the years taught. One account dates the first commercial wines to 2003: keep 1997 as the founding only with two sources. The Hedgehog single vineyard Xinomavro and its rosé go in others. Name no living founder.

picks.why: Estate begun in 2006 on the Amyndeon plateau and known above all for bottle fermented sparkling wine of Xinomavro; the Extra Cuvée de Réserve is its zero dosage blanc de noirs of ungrafted Xinomavro, left about five years on the lees by the house's own account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own sheet for the 2017 vintage, read through search: Xinomavro alone, ungrafted, zero dosage, a second fermentation in bottle and 54 to 84 months on the lees (five years by its terroir page), from vineyards in what the sheet calls a sub-region of the Amyndeo appellation; a Greek merchant places the vines at Agios Panteleimon, planted in 1970. IN DOUBT: whether the label carries PDO Amyndeon at all. The house's sheets title its Cuvée Spéciale a varietal sparkling wine and its rosé a varietal wine of Xinomavro and Limniona, and the appellation's sparkling wine is rosé by the Wines of Greece list of types, so a white sparkling wine may stand outside it: say what the label says and no more, and never call this wine the appellation's sparkling wine unless the label does. The house does bottle the appellation's own wine: a still red, Xinomavro Old Vines, sold as PDO Amyntaio by a British merchant, which goes in others first. 2006 is the founding by one merchant and the first vintage by another; the winery's village is Levea in one merchant's address and Filotas by a Greek travel site, so confirm it from the house. The Cuvée Spéciale (Xinomavro alone by one merchant, with a tenth of Assyrtiko by another), the Cuvée Rosé and the Cuvée Prestige go in others. The lane called the estate organic: confirm before saying so. Name no living founder.

picks.why: The growers' co-operative winery of Amyntaio town, at work since 1959 and since 2012 the winery of the Agricultural Cooperative of the Wider Amyntaio Area; its dry rosé of Xinomavro is the style Amyndeon alone holds as a PDO among the grape's appellations.

It is not the Amyntas rosé (Xinomavro with a fifth of Syrah, PGI Florina) and not the sparkling Rosé Demi Sec and Rosé Sec (the Sec by the closed tank method), which go in others; a Greek wine writer calls the Demi Sec the house's emblem. The label's wording in Latin letters was not seen: give the name as the bottle carries it, and tell the read together agent if it cannot hold the pick's words. The house's names by source: Coop. Amynteo (Wines of Greece), Amyntas Wines (its own address and the regional tourism body), the winery of the Union of Agricultural Cooperatives of Amyntaio before 2012, by the house. One glossary dates the co-operative itself to 1945 and the winery to 1959; the house dates its first sparkling trials to 1971 and the appellation to 1972. Shares and volumes stay out.

Confirm the founding (the restart of 2000 and the older family trade rest on one account: leave founded empty unless two agree), the village, the vineyard and the making of 7 Roots, and whether the house's older, oak aged Xinomavro has the stronger claim to be its flagship. Its blanc de noirs of Xinomavro, PGI Florina, goes in others.

picks.why: A winery on the outskirts of Agios Panteleimon, among the plateau's four lakes, written about in Greece and little seen abroad; its Xinomavro is a dry red of the grape alone under PDO Amyndeon, from vines of the village.

The author confirms the house, its founding and the wine's making from the house and a second source, or tells the merge agent, who may take the standby: Pavlou, an estate at Agios Panteleimon that worked with Xinomavro alone by an account of 2009, with a winery of 2006 and a red named Klima, which the same German glossary lists among the appellation's known houses but which no search of the thin run showed at work after about 2010. picks.why: Family winery in the town of Goumenissa, in its present form since 1978 by one account, with a family history of wine said to go back more than a century; its Goumenissa is the appellation's blend of Xinomavro and Negoska.

The author confirms which label is the one to know (the plain Goumenissa stands unless the single vineyard wine proves the one a guest meets), the founding (1978 for the present winery comes from one merchant and the earlier family date is unconfirmed: leave founded empty unless two agree) and whether the two grapes are fermented together, which the lane's why said the law asks and this run could not confirm. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Organic family estate at Filyria in the Goumenissa zone that works the appellation's blend and its grapes one by one; its Goumenissa is Xinomavro with about three parts in ten of Negoska.

Confirmed on this run: the Goumenissa carries the PDO and is stocked under this name in Greece and Britain as seven parts Xinomavro to three of Negoska, and the vineyards at Filyria are farmed organically by a Greek Master of Wine's account. The author confirms the certification and its year, the founding (1994 in one glossary, perhaps the planting and not the winery: leave founded empty unless two agree) and the label's spelling (Chatzivaritis on export labels, Chatzivariti and Hatzivaryti at Greek merchants). The varietal Negoska, the Xinomavro bottled alone and the Roditis go in others, none of them the appellation's wine. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Goumenissa family estate in its third generation, growing vines since 1924 by one account and farmed organically with little done in the cellar; its Goumenissa, first made in 1997 and released after long ageing, is the one met on natural wine lists abroad.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the Goumenissa carries the PDO (a natural wine fair's sheet for the 2009 and a second account), so the pick stands; the house's old vine Xinomavro has no Negoska and cannot carry it, and goes in others with the young vine red. The author confirms 1924 from two sources or leaves founded empty, the first vintage of 1997, the organic certification (1998 in one account) and the blend, given as equal parts in some vintages and seven to three in another: teach it without a fixed share. The lane's wild yeast, little sulphur and no filtration were not confirmed here. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: An older Goumenissa winery at the foot of Mount Paiko, taken over in 2018 by the founders of Ktima Biblia Chora and renamed; its Goumenissa is the classic blend of about four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed on this run: the estate is at Dyo Potamia by the northern winemakers' association's own page, its Goumenissa is stocked in Greece, Britain and Norway as four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska, and two accounts tell of the takeover, one of them giving 2018. The varietal Negoska goes in others. Name no living person of either house.

picks.why: The Macedonian house that took up Rapsani in 1991 and replanted the Olympus terraces with the local growers, for years the appellation's only producer, until it stopped production in 2023; its Rapsani Reserve, the three grapes fermented together and aged in oak, carried the name abroad for a generation.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Ruled at the merge of 16 November 2026: the house is closed (production stopped in September 2023 and its bankruptcy was entered in the commercial registry on 12 January 2026, by two Greek business reports found in the thin run), and it stands in this group as history, because its Reserve is the Rapsani a sommelier is asked about and meets in old bottles. Write the whole record in the past tense, confirm the closure and its dates from two sources, and say nothing of what becomes of the brand. Do not propose a swap for the closure. Confirm that Rapsani Reserve was the label's own wording (beside a Grande Reserve, which goes in others), the ageing each term asked from the PDO's own text, and the house's founding (1890 is commonly given) from two sources. Tell its work with the growers as history with its dates.

picks.why: Family winery at the foot of Olympus, at Rapsani since 1991 and farmed organically by several accounts; its Rapsani Old Vines is the appellation's three grapes from old vines, aged in oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: Rapsani Old Vines is sold as PDO Rapsani by a Canadian review site (the 2022), two British merchants (the 2019) and a Greek one, and a British critic's site reviewed the 2022; one merchant gives eighteen months in French and American oak and six in bottle, one account plants the vines in 1952, and a Greek travel site says Xinomavro can reach seven parts in ten of the blend. The house also bottles a plain Rapsani (the 2023 is on sale in Britain) and a Rapsani named Tourtoura Old Vines (the 2020 reviewed by the same critic's site): confirm from the house which is the wine to know, and send the others to others with the Meth'Imon wines, whose appellation the author confirms. The dates disagree and the author settles them: at Rapsani since 1991 by several listings, organic from 1997 by one, and bottling the appellation's wine since 2008 by another, so leave founded empty unless two agree on what 1991 was. The lane's site name (Prosilia) was not confirmed, and the altitude (550 to 700 metres by the listings) is the house's own. The Ministry of Rural Development's file of an application to amend the Rapsani specification, named for 30 July 2026 and seen only through search summaries, names this house's company: read it before writing the making or the grapes' shares. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Rapsani family estate whose first vineyard was planted about 1935 by its own account, with a small winery set up after the third generation took over in 2002; its Rapsani is the three grapes fermented together and aged a year in old oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house writes itself under a living man's name: a house keeps its name, but the prose names nobody. Confirmed in the thin run: the wine is sold as Rapsani by a Greek merchant and a British one (the 2021), and a British critic's site reviewed the 2019, the 2020 and the 2021 as Xinomavro, Krassato and Stavroto; the Greek merchant gives the three grapes fermented together and twelve months in old oak. About 1935 and the takeover of 2002 come from two merchants' profiles that read as the house's own words: hedge them as the house's account, and leave founded empty unless an independent source agrees. Sources write the house as Konstantinos Liapis, Liapis, Liapis Winery and Domaine Liapis: confirm the name the label carries, and that the label says PDO Rapsani. A Greek Master of Wine's account of 2016 has the head of this house working the vines of Terra Olympus, the Thymiopoulos company at Rapsani: say it only as two sources agree. Name no living person.

picks.why: The Rapsani company of the Naoussa house Thymiopoulos, set up about 2015 and, by one account, given its own cellar in a restored warehouse near Rapsani's railway station; Terra Petra is its Rapsani, Xinomavro with Krassato and Stavroto, sold under the Thymiopoulos name.
picks.note: Ruled at the merge of 16 November 2026: this pick stays under its own name, and the Naoussa note on Thymiopoulos points here. Thymiopoulos Vineyards is Naoussa's pick in plan.json (p-thymiopoulos), and that pick's note sends the Rapsani wine to others under the rule of one flagship a producer; the library's record of that house lists Rapsani Terra Petra among its wines. The company is entered here under its own name because three accounts make it a house of this appellation in its own right: a Greek Master of Wine's report of 2016 (the company is called Terra Olympus, and the 2016 vintage was to be made in its own winery in a restored warehouse near Rapsani's railway station), an importer's catalogue (established in 2015, when vineyards within the appellation came up for sale) and the Ministry of Rural Development's file of an application to amend the Rapsani specification, named for 30 July 2026 and seen only through a search summary, which names Terra Olympus of Rapsani. Keep producerId empty here. The wine is confirmed: Terra Petra is PDO Rapsani in an Austrian magazine's review of the 2015 and Rapsani in a British magazine's of the 2017 and the 2018, both under the Thymiopoulos name, and merchants in Greece and France stock the 2019 and the 2020. The author confirms what the label carries (Thymiopoulos, Terra Olympus or both), the grapes' shares (seven parts Xinomavro to three of Stavroto and Krassato by one Greek merchant, which sits beside the equal thirds the Codex's region record teaches: read the specification) and how the vines stand between this company and the Liapis family. Name no living person.

picks.why: A house at Rapsani's railway station, growing vines on Olympus since 1880 by its own account, known at home and little seen abroad; its Rapsani is the appellation's three grapes aged in oak, bottled beside a limited edition.

IN DOUBT, thin: no search of the thin run showed the house at work after about 2022, and no merchant's listing of a recent vintage was found. What was confirmed: a blog post of 2009 that reads as the house's own announcement (growing and making wine since 1880, a fourth generation, a Rapsani of Stavroto, Krassato and Xinomavro aged twelve months in French oak); a Tempi tourism site's page on the wine route (gotempi.gr), which lists it at Rapsani beside Dougos and Liapis; a Greek travel site's guide of about four years ago (two labels, a Rapsani PDO red and a Rapsani PDO special edition, both aged in oak, and the address at Rapsani's railway station); and a Greek Master of Wine's note on the Rapsani 2009 Limited Edition, tasted in January 2020. The author confirms from the house that it bottles today, the label's own words and spelling (Chrisohoou in two sources, Chrysochoou in others), 1880 from a second source or leaves founded empty, and the blend. It is not the Chrysohoou estate of Naoussa, a different house whose wines turn up in the same searches. Tsantali, closed since 2023, stands in this group as history by the ruling at the merge. The only other bottler found is Boutari, whose own site lists a Rapsani of 2022, and Boutari is Naoussa's pick. Katsaros, which one glossary lists here, is at Krania, which has its own PGI. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: A house begun in 1986 at Pyrgela outside Argos and settled since 2004 in a winery at Malandreni, one of the two Argolid communes of the Nemea zone; the Grande Cuvée, Agiorgitiko alone from high vineyards and first bottled in 1996 by the house's account, is its Nemea.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own pages (skouras.gr, read through search): founded in 1986 at Pyrgela, a village outside Argos, with rented vineyards; then a small winery at Gymno; then the winery at Malandreni in 2004, both villages inside the appellation, which Wines of Greece bears out (seventeen communes, fifteen in Corinthia with Gymno and Malandreni in Argolida). The house's sheet gives the wine as PDO Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone, first bottled in 1996, from vineyards at 1,040 metres; an American importer's listing adds red clay and twelve months in French barriques, half of them new. The vine age differs by merchant and the village of the vineyard was not found: confirm both from the technical sheet of the year taught. The label's word order varies on the house's own pages (Grande Cuvée Nemea on one, Nemea Grande Cuvée on another), so the pick holds Grande Cuvée alone, where the lane held Grande Cuvée Nemea: give the label in full. Megas Oenos, the first wine the house made, a blend of Agiorgitiko and Cabernet Sauvignon outside the appellation, goes in others with Saint George, its other Nemea. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate at Ancient Nemea, by its merchants' accounts at work with Agiorgitiko since 1876 and among the district's first to farm organically; Palaia Klimata, Old Vines on the export label, is Agiorgitiko alone from an old section of its vineyard, held long in oak and bottle.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own label pages (papaioannouwines.gr, read through search): Palaia Klimata, Old Vines in English and Vieilles Vignes in French, Nemea PDO, Agiorgitiko alone, made at the family winery at Ancient Nemea from a chosen section of vines about forty years old, with eighteen months in oak and a year in bottle; a British merchant gives at least twelve months in French oak and twelve in bottle, so tell the regime by vintage. The house's German page spells it Palea Klimata. The year 1876 and the early organic farming come from merchants and Greek guides, not from a house page seen: hedge 1876 as a claim or leave founded empty, and confirm the certification before saying certified. Microclima, as the house spells its Nemea from a single plot, goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Nemea estate of the Mantinia house Tselepos: a vineyard of old Agiorgitiko at Koutsi bought in 2003 and named Ktima Driopi, with a small winery of its own; the Reserve, Agiorgitiko alone with a year in French oak, is its Nemea for the cellar.

Confirmed in the thin run on the family's own pages (tselepos.gr, read through search): 2003 is the purchase of the estate at Koutsi and the founding of Ktima Driopi; the vines were about fifty years old by the house (thirty five by one merchant), a part was replanted with clean Agiorgitiko and a small winery was built on the estate. The house lists the wine as Ktima Driopi Reserve, Nemea PDO, Agiorgitiko alone, twelve months in French oak, seven tenths of it new, and six months in bottle, from a vineyard it places at Dourmiza in Koutsi. The spelling is Driopi on the house's pages and Dryopi at a Greek merchant. The house gives the estate 380 metres and an American merchant about 1,250 feet: use the house's figure. The same family as the Mantinia pick Tselepos: a separate estate with its own name and wine, which the record says plainly. Driopi Classic, Cava Driopi and the rosé go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family winery at Petri, begun in 1997 by two accounts and in 1996 by a third, its vines farmed without irrigation or fertiliser; Monopati, the first of its premium wines, is Agiorgitiko alone under the appellation, aged in French oak.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: Monopati is sold as PDO Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone, by a Greek merchant and written up as Nemea by a Greek Master of Wine and on a British critic's site (the 2021: vines at 550 metres, twenty five days on the skins). The lane's 1996 is one merchant's year; a Greek food guide and the Greek Master of Wine give 1997: leave founded empty unless the house settles it. The vineyard: one plot at Daouliza in Koutsi since the 2014 vintage and Sikitsa before it, by the Master of Wine's notes; vines more than fifty years old by one merchant and nearing fifty by another: confirm both. The oak is fourteen or sixteen months in French barrels by vintage, and the wine is unfiltered by one listing. Whether the vineyard is certified organic is contested between listings: say dry farmed and no more. The wine named 4, from a vineyard said to predate phylloxera, Le Sang de la Pierre, Armakas and the estate Nemea go in others; confirm that Monopati and not 4 is the wine a guest meets. A father founded the house and his son, trained in Burgundy, makes the wine: name neither.

picks.why: Family winery founded in 1995 at Ancient Nemea, a short walk from the sanctuary, with a range that runs from a plain Nemea to regional blends; Ammos Terra Leone is its oak aged Nemea, Agiorgitiko alone from the family's own vineyard at Kokkinies.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; the region record's producers line names the house, a lead and no proof. Added in the thin run as the fifth pick, because Gaia Wines is Santorini's pick and Semeli is Mantinia's. Confirmed on the house's own pages (palivos.gr, read through search): a family winery founded in 1995 at Ancient Nemea, when a modern winery took the place of the old treading tank, 800 metres from the archaeological site; Ammos Terra Leone is a dry red PDO Nemea of Agiorgitiko alone from the family's vineyard at Kokkinies and Stefani. A British merchant and a Greek wine magazine also date the house to 1995; one account says the vineyards had been the family's for a century and a half: hedge it. The label's words vary: Ammos Terra Leone on the house's pages and at a British merchant for the 2022, Terra Leone Ammos Reserve on a British critic's site for the 2020, Terra Leone Single Vineyard Selection Ammos Reserve in an Austrian magazine for the 2006, so the pick holds Terra Leone alone: give the label in full for the years taught, and say Reserve only where the label does. The ageing differs between the house's two pages (eighteen months in French oak and six in bottle; fourteen months in new French oak and amphorae and eight in bottle) and a merchant gives the 2014 eighteen months in new oak, four fifths French and a fifth American: tell it by vintage. Noema, the house's blend of Agiorgitiko, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, is PGI Peloponnese and never its Nemea; it goes in others with Palivou Estate Nemea, the plain wine of the appellation. The house writes Palivou in English and Palivos in its address. Organic and biodynamic farming is a merchant's word: confirm before saying so. A founder and his two daughters appear on the house's pages: name none of them. Should a pick fall, the standby is the Nemea Wine Cooperative, founded in 1937 by retailers' accounts, whose Nemea Grande Reserve a British grocer sells as PDO: not confirmed on a page of its own.

Dafni and the old vine Liatiko of the Aggelis vineyard go in others; Dafni may be argued the flagship, so choose one with two sources. Name no living member of the family.

picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is given as 1984 in one source: confirm from two or leave it empty. Confirm the label form (Cellar Selection Wild Ferment), the vineyard, its altitude and the PDO; Wild Paths goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the flagship (Vostilidi, or the house's Robola of Cephalonia) and its label, the village and the founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.producer: Union of Winemaking Cooperatives of Samos
picks.why: The growers' co-operative union founded in 1934, the appellation's only producer until 2016 by Wines of Greece, with wineries at Malagari and Karlovasi; Samos Vin Doux, small grained White Muscat fortified with grape spirit, is the bottle any server meets.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; the region record's producers line names the house, a lead and no proof. Confirmed in the thin run: 1934 on the co-operative's own history page (samoswine.gr, read through search) and at Wines of Greece, which adds that it began with twenty six local co-operatives and that it was the only producer of the appellation until 2016, private wineries working beside it since; the island's wine routes guide names its two wineries, at Malagari by the town of Samos and at Karlovasi. Samos Vin Doux is listed under that name by a British magazine and a Canadian critic. The house's name differs by source: Union of Vinicultural Cooperatives of Samos (EOSS) at Wines of Greece, United Winemaking Agricultural Cooperative of Samos or UWC Samos in the wine routes guide and on the listings; the pick keeps the name the region record uses: give the name the label prints, and say when the union took its later form only if two sources date it. Wines of Greece gives the appellation three types: vin naturellement doux from sun dried grapes, vin doux naturel, fortified, with Grand Cru for fruit grown above 400 metres, and vin doux; that the Vin Doux is a vin de liqueur, fortified at or near the start of fermentation, rests on the region record and one taster's note: confirm it on the appellation's specification. Grand Cru, Nectar, of sun dried grapes, and Anthemis, aged in oak, go in others. Shares, volumes and exports stay out.

picks.why: Family winery at Karlovasi, opened in 2013 by the island's wine routes guide and a merchant's account, of a family that came from Malta in the nineteenth century and traded the island's Muscat; Nopera Vintage is its sweet Samos of sun dried Muscat.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: the island's wine routes guide (samoswineroutes.gr, read through search) places the winery at Karlovasi, dates its opening to 2013 and tells of a family that left Malta in the middle of the nineteenth century, made wine of White Muscat on Samos and later traded it abroad; a merchant's page also gives 2013, as the year the house became the first modern private winery. No page of the house's own was reached: hedge the family's story as the house's account, and leave founded empty unless 2013 stands on the house's own page. That it was the first private winery of Samos since 1934 is the guide's and that merchant's line, and Vakakis is dated 2011: hedge it or leave it out. Nopera Vintage is sold under that name by a Greek merchant (the 2013) and by a British importer of Greek wine (the 2017: ripe Muscat dried in the sun, then fermented slowly), and listings place it under PDO Samos; a Greek Master of Wine's site lists it as Nopera with the year alone and gives the 2014 about two years in French oak, and a British magazine lists it as Nopera, Samos: give the label in full for the year taught and confirm the appellation on it. Epitome, the house's other sweet wine, and Roya, its dry Muscat, which the lane held to be a wine of geographical indication outside the sweet appellation, go in others; confirm what Epitome is, since one listing runs it together with the Vintage of 2013, and confirm Roya's category. The guide's three vineyards and their size stay out. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Private winery near Karlovasi that began in 2011, while the law of 1934 still bound the island's growers to the co-operatives; Epogdoon, its Samos of partly sun dried White Muscat, is named for the interval of nine to eight in the Pythagorean theory of music.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Confirmed in the thin run: two accounts, a Greek merchant's and a tour guide's, date the house to 2011, when the law of 1934 still obliged the island's growers to deliver their grapes to the co-operatives, and say its founder fought that rule in the Greek and the European courts: tell the lawsuit only with a source that names the case, and say what the house bottled before 2016, which no search showed. The village differs by source: the island's wine routes guide places the winery at M. Lakka, on the road from Karlovasi to Konteika, and a travel guide files it under Vathy: follow the wine routes guide. Epogdoon is listed as PDO by a British merchant (the 2016, Muscat Blanc alone) and under Samos on a British critic's site (the 2017, there called Pythagorean Epogdoon Barrel): a barrel aged bottling stands beside the plain one, so say which is taught and give the label in full. The name, by the Greek merchant quoting the house: the epogdoon is the interval of nine to eight on which the Pythagorean theory of music rests, chosen for a partly sun dried wine of White Muscat; the same page says about eight kilos of fruit give one litre: confirm both on the house's own page. The lane's line that the house is known for reviving Black Muscat was not tested: say it only with two sources. Filion, listed under Samos on the same critic's site, and Kalypso go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family winery at Marathokampos, at work since 2016 among the terraces of the family's estate; its Samos, sold under the appellation's name alone, is a naturally sweet wine of sun dried White Muscat aged at least three years in barrel, by the house's account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Added in the thin run as the fourth pick. Confirmed on the house's own pages (coutsodontiswinery.gr, read through search): small lots made since 2016 on a family estate at Marathokampos among traditional terraces; the wine is headed Samos Naturally Sweet Wine in English and Samos, oinos fysikos glykys, in Greek, the 2017 of Muscat Blanc from small terraces at 100 to 300 metres, the grapes laid in the sun before pressing, fermented in stainless steel and aged at least three years in barrels. The island's wine routes guide also dates the family winery to 2016 and places it at Marathokampos. No merchant, critic or competition listing of the wine was found, so the record would rest on the house's pages alone: hedge every figure as the house's account. The letters PDO were not seen: the page gives the appellation's name and the legal words for its sun dried type, which Wines of Greece lists under PDO Samos, so confirm the appellation on the label before the record says it. The pick holds Samos alone because the wine has no other name: give the label in full. Its dry White Muscat, its aged dry White Muscat, its orange wine and its pétillant naturel go in others: confirm each one's category, since none can be the sweet appellation's wine. The house writes Coutsodontis; a Greek news guide writes Koutsodontis. No listing off the island was found: the record says plainly that this is a small young house, little seen abroad on what was read. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Young family estate at Mytilinii in the centre of the island, founded in 2019, farming organically and making only White Muscat, dry and naturally sweet; Anavasis is the wine it bottles as Samos, young and from a wild ferment by a merchant's listing.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. Added in the thin run as the fifth pick, and the one in doubt. Confirmed: the island's wine routes guide (samoswineroutes.gr, read through search) dates the winery to 2019 at Rizovrachos, Mytilinii, in central Samos, a father and his two sons working organic vineyards and making only dry and naturally sweet wines of White Muscat in numbered bottles; the estate's own page (hatziioannouestate.gr, read through search) calls it a family house given wholly to organic wines. Anavasis: the results of the Concours Mondial de Bruxelles list Hatziioannou, Samos, Anavasis 2021 as a still wine of Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, appellation Samos, organic and not oaked; a wine app names it Samos with the wine's name in Greek; a delicatessen that sells the island's wines online lists Anabasis in a half litre bottle as an organic Samos, young and fermented by native yeasts alone. No page read says PDO or sweet of this wine outright: the case rests on the name Samos on the label, which only the appellation's wine may carry, on the competition's appellation field, on the half litre bottle and on the estate's naturally sweet wines. Confirm on the estate's own page or the label that Anavasis is PDO Samos and which of the appellation's types it is; if it is not, the pick falls. Antamoma, also written Rendezvous, its dry White Muscat, goes in others. The spelling is Anavasis at the competition and Anabasis at the delicatessen; the house is Hatziioannou on its own pages and Hatzigiannou in a Greek news guide, and a retailer's dry Muscat of Chatziioannou Domaine may be the same estate or another house: keep them apart until shown. The medal stays out. Name no living member of the family. Should the pick fall, no sixth house of the appellation was found: of the seven the wine routes guide lists, Kostaki, whose first vintage was 2023, makes dry and sparkling Muscat by a Greek merchant and a British magazine, and nothing was found on the wines of Eleftheriou at Stavrinides; the Samos bottled by the mainland houses Kourtaki and Cavino, seen in Canadian listings, was not tested and is a label from off the island.

picks.why: The Keuka Lake house founded in 1962 as Vinifera Wine Cellars by a Ukrainian born plant scientist who showed that grafted vinifera could live through Finger Lakes winters; its Dry Riesling is the bottle that carried that argument.
picks.note: Confirm the founding as Vinifera Wine Cellars in 1962 from the house and a second source, and the Dry Riesling's sources of fruit for the years taught. The Rkatsiteli and the Chateau Frank sparkling wines go in others. Name the founder only with his dates from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Seneca Lake estate founded at Dundee in 1979 by a Mosel born grower, whose nursery grafted vines for growers across the East; the HJW Vineyard Riesling, the single vineyard wine that carries the founder's initials, is the house's Riesling to know.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 1979 (the library's), the HJW Vineyard's place and the wine's style by vintage (dry or with a little sweetness) from the house and a second source; the Dry Riesling and the Magdalena Vineyard Riesling go in others. Whether the founder is living is not settled here: name him only if two sources give his death with its date, else say the founder.

picks.why: A Keuka Lake house making Riesling and Cabernet Franc in a dry, restrained style from Keuka and Seneca fruit; the Argetsinger Vineyard Dry Riesling, from one of the old vineyards of Seneca Lake, on limestone, is the one to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (2000 or 2001 by different accounts) and the Argetsinger Vineyard's shore, age and soils from the house and a second source; one review alone was read here for the site. Name no living person: say the founding couple.

picks.why: A vineyard on the east shore of Seneca Lake given almost wholly to Riesling and bottled by clone and by sweetness; No. 239 Dry Riesling is a single clone wine of Geisenheim clone 239, a lesson in what a clone brings to a glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the planting year and the vineyard's place from the house. The wines have been made at other Seneca Lake wineries, by different accounts at different houses in different years: teach the vineyard as the house and name no cellar as its maker without two sources. Name no living person.

picks.why: A Seneca Lake house founded with a partner from the southern Rhône, making bone dry Riesling and Pinot Noir in a European idiom; the Classique Dry Riesling, blended from sites on the east shore of the lake, is its wine to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (2011 by most accounts) and the partners from the house and a second source, naming none: the Rhône partner's own house, Château de Saint Cosme, is wave one's Southern Rhône pick, and Forge Cellars is a separate house. Confirm the label form (Dry Riesling Classique on some listings) and the sites it blends; the single vineyard Rieslings and the Classique Pinot Noir go in others.

picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year and Musée's grapes for the years taught from the house and a second source, and confirm any account of artists' labels before teaching it. The Merlot and the Taste wines go in others. Name no living person.

picks.why: Peconic estate planted in 1978, one of the early vineyards of the North Fork; its long aged Merlot from the old vines is the wine that first set Long Island beside Bordeaux at blind tastings.

Confirm the planting year 1978, the release after long ageing and the blind tastings against Bordeaux, with their dates and wines, from the house and a second source, or leave the tastings out. The Old Vines Chardonnay, the Old Vines Cabernet Sauvignon and the sparkling Cuvée go in others. Name no living person.

picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the planting from 1988 and the founder's dates (he died in 2008 by recollection) from two sources before naming him. picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt between Bergen Road and Alexandra, the house's reserve red by one listing: confirm from the house which it leads with, and the blend for the years taught; the Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc go in others. Confirm the planting year and the biodynamic farming from two sources. Name no living member of the family.

Confirm the founding year 1976, the ruins (the house Jefferson designed for James Barbour, burnt in the nineteenth century) and Octagon's name, blend and the years it is made from the house and a second source. Say the Veneto family, name no living member. Its Italian grapes go in others.

picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the first Viognier vintage and the competition an early vintage won (1993 by one account) from two sources; the Norton, the Petit Manseng and the Rkatsiteli go in others. Whether the founder is living is not settled here: say the founder, name no one.

picks.why: A Blue Ridge estate in Fauquier County known for wines drawn from its own mountain slopes; the Hardscrabble Chardonnay, from the home vineyard of that name, is the house's white to know, beside a Hardscrabble red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick open between the Hardscrabble Chardonnay and the Hardscrabble red blend: teach the one the house leads with, the other in others. Confirm the founding year and the Hardscrabble site from the house and a second source. Name no living person: say the grower who founded it.

picks.why: A Delaplane estate in the Blue Ridge foothills of northern Virginia making two Bordeaux style reds from its own slopes; Lost Mountain, the Cabernet Sauvignon led one, is the house's flagship.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; not in the region record. Pick in doubt: one source read here gives Lost Mountain to another house. Confirm from the house's own pages that Lost Mountain is its Cabernet Sauvignon led wine and Rendezvous its other, and the first vintage and the site's soils from two sources. Name no living person: say the founder.

picks.why: A northern Virginia estate given to Norton, the native grape raised in Richmond in the 1820s, and to Albariño; its Norton is the state's own red grape in an estate's hands.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label (Locksley Reserve Norton by recollection, not confirmed by any source read here) and which Norton the house leads with, from the house and a second source; the Albariño and the Viognier go in others. Name no living person: say the founder.

picks.why: Molinos estate in the upper Calchaquí, founded in 1831 and one of Argentina's oldest working wineries; Altura Máxima, Malbec from a vineyard at roughly 3,100 metres, puts the altitude of the Calchaquí in one bottle.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 1831 (the library's) and the vineyard's height (roughly 3,100 metres in the region record) from the house and a second source. The Estate Malbec and the Torrontés go in others; teach Altura Máxima as the flagship only if the house presents it so, else ask the merge agent for the Estate Malbec. Ownership is told only as history with its year; name no living person.

picks.why: Cafayate house founded in 1892, the valley's historic cellar, with old vines of Torrontés, Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon; the Old Vines 1945 Torrontés, named for the year its parcel was planted, shows the valley's grape from old vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding in 1892 (the region record) and the founders from the house and a second source, and that 1945 is the parcel's planting year. The house was long known by another name by one account: tell the change as history with its year if two sources agree. The red blends and the other Old Vines wines go in others. Present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A long established Cafayate house, revived in 1938 by the Etchart family and a name for Torrontés in dry and late harvest styles; Arnaldo B., the red named for the man who revived it, is the house's flagship.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The dates 1850 and 1938 and a first vintage of 1990 come from a retailer: confirm from the house and a second source or leave them out, and name Arnaldo Benito Etchart only with his dates. San Pedro de Yacochuya is the family's later estate and a separate house, its own pick. The sale of the house out of the family is history only with its year from two sources. The Torrontés wines go in others.

picks.why: Small estate in the hills above Cafayate at about 2,000 metres, begun in 1988 by the Etchart family with a Bordeaux consultant; Yacochuya is its dense Malbec from old vines, one of Argentina's early wines made for the cellar.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the start (1988) and the first release (1990 by one account), the vineyard's height (6,700 feet by one account) and the vines' age (60 years by one account, over a century by another) from two sources, or leave them out. The consultant is living: say a Bordeaux consultant, never his name. The San Pedro de Yacochuya red and the Torrontés go in others. Bodegas Etchart, of the same family's history, is its own pick.

picks.why: A restored historic family cellar in Cafayate making Torrontés and reds of Malbec and Tannat from the valley's sandy soils; Laborum names its single vineyard wines, its Torrontés the house's white to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt: Laborum is given from recollection and no source read in this roster confirmed it. Confirm from the house that Laborum names its single vineyard wines and which of them it leads with (a Torrontés or a Malbec), else propose a swap. Confirm the cellar's age and the family's tenure from two sources. Name no living person, its consultant included.

picks.why: San Juan's historic house, founded in the province in 1870 by an Italian immigrant; the Centenario Malbec, a reserve range, is the label by which the old name is met on lists.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is 1870 by most accounts and 1869 by one: confirm from the house and a second source, and name Santiago Graffigna only with his dates. Confirm the label form (Centenario Reserve Malbec by one listing), its fruit and whether the house leads with it or with its Grand Reserve. A change of ownership in 2019 by one source is history only with two sources; present ownership is volatile.

picks.why: A Tulum Valley house founded in 1993 that carried San Juan Syrah onto export lists; the Gran Syrah, blended from the Tulum, Zonda and Pedernal valleys, is its flagship and the province's grape at full stretch.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year 1993 and the three valleys of the Gran Syrah from the house and a second source. Present ownership is volatile: leave it out. The Reserva range and the Malbec go in others.

picks.why: A San Juan estate built around Syrah, whose warm valley wines made the province's grape familiar abroad; its Syrah is San Juan's warm style in the glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Pick in doubt on the wine: no source read in this roster named Callia's leading label. Confirm from the house which Syrah it leads with and keep Syrah in the name, else propose a swap. Sources disagree on whether its fruit is Tulum or Pedernal and on its owner: confirm the vineyards from two sources and leave ownership out. Callia and Pyros belong to one group by one account: teach them as two houses only if each keeps its own cellar and vineyards.

picks.why: A Pedernal Valley estate at about 1,400 metres on the province's high western side, showing what altitude does for San Juan Malbec and Syrah; the Vineyard Block No. 4 Malbec, from one block of the estate, is its wine to know.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label form (Vineyard Block No. 4 on one review listing, printed with the numero sign), the block's height and soils and the house's founding year from the house and a second source; the Appellation Malbec and Syrah go in others. See Callia's note on the group both belong to by one account.

picks.why: A small project at Barreal in the Calingasta Valley, bottling old pergola Criolla and other heritage grapes from smallholders' vineyards under the Andes; its Criolla is the old mission grape of the Spanish made as a light, fresh red.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label (Cara Sur Criolla, or Criolla Chica by name) and which Criolla it is, from the house and a second source; the house's name is said to be a mountain face: confirm which before teaching it. One founding partner is of the family of Familia Zuccardi, wave one's Mendoza pick: Cara Sur is a separate project, and none of its founders is named, all being living. The Bonarda and the Moscatel go in others.

picks.why: Mainque estate in the Río Negro founded in 2004 around abandoned own rooted Pinot Noir and farmed biodynamically; Treinta y Dos, from the vines planted in 1932 and named for the year, showed that Argentina had more than Malbec to give.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year 2004, the parcel's planting year 1932 and the biodynamic farming from the house and a second source. Cincuenta y Cinco and Barda go in others. The founder is of the family behind Tenuta San Guido, wave one's Bolgheri pick: Chacra is a separate house; say the family, name no living member.

picks.why: The historic Alto Valle house at General Roca, making wine since the early twentieth century; its Old Vineyard Sémillon, from the estate's old vines, is the Patagonian white a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is given as 1909 and as 1914 by different sources: confirm from the house and a second source or leave it empty, and name the founder only with his dates.
